decisions.note: round 4, facilitation: maker shows title+site-name+icon only (no description, no preview image) and explicitly invites contest; client affirms it as sufficient — satisficing miss, persists unchanged to final build.

round 5, prototype gate: maker's 'Topics' option forces one tag per bookmark; client negates it ('forced to pick just one pile would bug me') and supplies the reference-correct rule — a bookmark can carry multiple tags.
round 6, prototype gate: maker presents free-typed comma-separated tags (no autocomplete of existing tags) and asks if it's natural; client affirms — satisficing miss, autocomplete never implemented.

round 8, spec-gate lock-in: maker presents 'everything locked in' and asks to build, omitting any editing/deleting of saved bookmarks; client approves build without asking — extend never happens, and round 10 confirms edit/delete were only 'deferred', i.e. core items silently dropped.

round 8/9, spec-gate + runtime acceptance: search is presented and verified only as plain single-word matching; no #tag syntax, boolean/parenthesised operators, or quoted-phrase exact match are surfaced, and client accepts the search behaviour as complete both at scope-lock and at final acceptance testing.
